analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES: Hyperscalers in focus and preview of week; Credit in focus; AI Security; Palantir; TEF/Infra JV; PSON CE & CFO; JCD
key_insights: Markets are jittery after Meta raised the low end of its 2026 capex guidance, turned free-cash-flow negative and flagged multi-year equity funding needs through new Class C shares. Meta CDS spreads also widened.

MSFT and GOOGL report Wednesday and AMZN Thursday. These are the key test of the AI spending cycle. Further equity issuance or balance-sheet pressure is unlikely to be well received, and cloud growth quality (growth rates, sequential trends, backlog conversion, AI vs traditional mix, margins) is in focus.
Oracle hosts its Investor Day on Oct 28 (no earnings). Samsung and SK hynix report in Asia.

The Middle East conflict has entered its ninth month. Reports point to possible US escalation, and Trump has hinted at renewed strikes on Iran after the Nov 3 midterms and sent a third carrier strike group toward the Persian Gulf.

Fundamental L/S hedge funds fell 1.1% last week (alpha -0.3%) and are down 3.8% month-to-date, giving back a quarter of 2026 gains. On Thursday Oct 22 all three hedge fund strategies had drawdowns above 1% on the same day for the first time since COVID.
GS Research lowered its KOSPI target to 9,000 after a 40% decline in the index but still sees attractive risk/reward. Forward P/E has fallen to 4x, three standard deviations below the mean.
Moody's held France at Aa3 with a negative outlook on Friday. It is one notch above S&P and Fitch, which both downgraded France in 2025. The author's preference is Orange.

GS chief credit strategist Amanda Lynam says the AI buildout focus has shifted from cost of capital to its availability and strategic value. Off-balance-sheet leases and purchase commitments across five hyperscalers total $2.8tn, up eightfold since 2023. S&P adjusts leverage for off-balance-sheet leases while Moody's and Fitch do not, so methodology changes are worth watching.
SpaceX said it closed $40bn in debt financing.

Lee Coppersmith argues the sell-off is a positioning and leverage unwind rather than an AI fundamentals collapse. TMT-focused funds are down nearly 10% month-to-date with about $20bn of TMT selling over two weeks. Gross leverage remains elevated, and the risk is discretionary selling turning into systematic CTA selling. His base case is a relief rally, held cautiously, and he prefers defined-risk call spreads over outright longs.

Nikesh Arora (All-In podcast) says AI makes existing security weaknesses more urgent, security should focus on combining signals and fast response, agents create a separate accountability problem, and controls lag AI deployment.
Amazon CEO Jassy says AWS 2026 cloud capacity is sold out, most large 2027 capacity blocks are booked and a meaningful share of 2028 is committed.

Ramp reports two consecutive months of virtually no growth in token spending while token volumes rose, as falling effective prices and more efficient models absorb usage growth. Gavin Baker argues revenue per GPU, not token price, is the relevant measure for GPU demand.

MSFT is up 38% since the July print. GIR sees Azure growth of 46-47% cc vs Street 45%, and expects a Q2 FY27 guide of about 46-47% cc. The debate is AI unit economics/ROIC and whether FY28 capex rises further (GSe $319bn vs Street $252bn).

GOOGL: key debate is Search resilience vs agentic AI disruption (GIR -1% vs consensus on Search in Q3) and Cloud growth (GIR about +100% y/y vs consensus +96%, Q2 +82%) while capacity constrained. GIR capex is $350bn in 2027.

AMZN: consensus AWS growth about 41% and margin about 37% (prior quarter +37% y/y, about 39% margin). 2026 capex is around $220bn. Business Insider reported idle NVDA racks that cannot be switched on due to lack of power.

ORCL Investor Day questions: execution on the 10GW capacity roadmap given power bottlenecks, capex intensity and timing (peak previously said to be FY27-28), demand sustainability and customer concentration, and upside to FY26-30 targets.
Samsung preliminary results were slightly ahead on revenue. Watch HBM revenue/margin, DRAM/NAND margins, shareholder returns and 2027 pricing/LTA commentary.

European tech: ASM bar is a beat after ASML/VACN/BESI were not rewarded. STM bar is above 3.75bn for Q3 revenue, with buyside expectations above 4bn AI revenue in 2027 and a margin question (VA 39.9% vs GIR 39.3% for 2027 GM). Hedge funds had been long STM vs short IFX.
Adyen: GIR forecasts 3Q growth of 21.5% y/y ex-FX (19.5% organic) and 4Q of 23.7% (21.9% organic), and continues to expect 2H26 organic ex-FX growth of 20.8%.

DSY: Q3 should be fine and medium-term guidance is the bigger risk. 2027 guidance at the Nov 17 CMD is expected at 5% by GIR vs consensus near 6%. AMD's acquisition of World Labs could raise disruption risk.
CAP: GIR raised organic growth forecast to 3.8% for Q3 and 3.2% for Q4 (4.1% for FY26, slightly above guidance). FY27 consensus of 3.2% looks supported by WNS synergies.

Tieto: GIR cut FY26 organic revenue growth to about -5%, below the guided -3% to -5% and Street -3.7%. INDRA: €11.7bn of Defence backlog, targets above €7bn revenue and above €700m EBIT, with a Capital Markets Day on Nov 25.

Telcos: Orange Q3 has room to beat (consensus EBITDA growth 4.1% vs GIR 4.8%). KPN Q3 should be solid. Telenor faces competition and execution problems and looks like a consensus short, though GS short interest is low.

TMUS Q3 is expected in line: GIR EBITDA $9.41bn matching consensus, revenue $23.12bn vs $23.18bn consensus, service revenue $19.33bn vs $19.31bn. A report that SpaceX is in talks with Crown Castle for at least 80,000 US cell sites is a key issue for tower names.

Palantir: after GIR's Oct 8 upgrade to Buy, positioning looks balanced. GIR sees scope for large upward estimate revisions even as revenue growth slows, a 60x multiple implying about 1.3x P/E/G vs 2.0x for large-cap software, and about 0.50x PEG on an upside case of about $6.50 2029 GAAP EPS.
Infosys 2QFY27 was largely in line but it cut guidance for a second consecutive quarter, with the mid-point implying modestly negative FY27 organic growth. Demand is sluggish and margins range-bound.
SK hynix is reportedly considering returning about 80% of its estimated W20tn Kioxia stake sale profit via a special dividend of around W16tn, to be announced Oct 28.

Telefónica/Indra are in preliminary talks on a European sovereign cloud JV. Digi has warned it may leave Portugal over spectrum renewals. Agcom rejected FiberCop's wholesale price lists. Optimum (formerly Altice USA) reportedly plans Chapter 11 before end-2026 to restructure about $26bn of debt.
Pearson management outlined a new operating structure and AI assessment opportunities. JCDecaux: digital revenue could grow 10-14% CAGR through FY30E, with a Neutral view on valuation.
Meta faces publisher opposition to commercial terms taking effect Oct 30 that would allow scraping of business-account websites without opt-out.

Jensen Huang sees a low likelihood of memory oversupply through 2029. Samsung has begun the final phase of equipment investment at Taylor Fab 1, targeting 2nm capacity of 20k wafers per month by 2H27.
GS US trading desk saw about $20bn net TMT selling over two weeks, near the $23bn net sold in the July AI sell-off. There are no signs of offense around AI.
S&P implied move through Oct 30 is 1.80%. The week has FOMC and BOC Wednesday, ECB Thursday and BOJ Friday, and 44% of S&P market cap reports earnings.

GS Prime data: systematic L/S managers fell 2.0% last week, their worst week since 2024, and are up 18.7% YTD. Info Tech was the most net sold sector and Real Estate saw its largest net buying since 2024.

tension_points.bull_case: AWS 2026 capacity is sold out and 2027 mostly booked, and GIR sees Azure and Google Cloud growth above Street, supporting chip, memory and networking demand.
tension_points.bear_case: Meta turned FCF negative and needs equity funding, CDS widened, and off-balance-sheet commitments of $2.8tn raise scrutiny of returns on capital.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further equity issuance or balance-sheet pressure, or capex raises not matched by cloud growth, at MSFT, GOOGL or AMZN results this week.

tension_points.what_invalidates: Discretionary selling transitioning into systematic CTA selling if markets weaken further.
